notes: No numbeo.com page was opened. Evidence comes from restaurant menus (HTML and text-layer PDFs, autumn 2026), operator fare pages, supermarket catalogue aggregators and a few travel guides; 22 WebSearch calls were used. Pattern: the LivingCost-derived mealMid2 values for ZRH, PAR and REK are far below real menus, and the beerShop values for French and Swiss cities (and HEL) are 40-100 percent above shelf and catalogue prices. None of my cities has mealMid2 below 2x mealCheap (lowest ratio ZRH 2.74 before the fix). Not changed but worth a look: GVA and BSL mealMid2 (EUR 118 and 112) look low-side, because Les Armures in Geneva (Oct 2026: starters CHF 9-30, mains CHF 26-56, desserts CHF 12-15) and Safran Zunft in Basel (Oct 2026: three-course menu CHF 89, mains CHF 30-72) imply roughly CHF 120-160 for two, so the whole crowd-sourced mealMid2 level in expensive cities may be 15-30 percent under menu prices; I only fixed values that were clearly out of line. HEL beerShop is the least certain correction. GLA transit relies on First Bus's GBP 2 cap started on 7 Sep 2026 with no stated end date (Subway single GBP 1.80). VNO transit matches the 30-minute ticket only (60-minute EUR 1.25). Vienna's 3.00 is the digital price (EUR 3.20 at machines since 1 Jan 2026). Source prices are in local currency converted with 2026-12-europe/fx.json (GBP 0.84763, CHF 0.9313, ISK 136.8 per EUR).
